text:
The best match for the farm's future climate in the 2050s is Garfield County, Washington, featuring a strong match quality with 8 out of 8 climate models in agreement. Lower sigma means the place's climate today is closer to the farm's future climate. 

Looking at crop rotations, 3 matching areas use the field's current rotation of Winter wheat to Fallow. Other rotations used at the matching places include Winter wheat to Spring wheat to Fallow, a flexible mix of fallow and winter wheat, and a flexible mix of fallow, spring wheat, and winter wheat.

Comparing hazards with the best match in Garfield County, the field today has 37 days above 32 degrees Celsius per year compared to 42 for the match, 165 frost-free days compared to 198, a June afternoon ground temperature of 37.9 degrees Celsius compared to 40.5, a July-August afternoon ground temperature of 45.6 degrees Celsius compared to 45.9, and driest-month soil water in September of 16.9 percent compared to 21.3 percent.

Across the middle-of-the-road emissions scenario, temperatures and precipitation are projected to shift over the coming decades.

Candidates were evaluated using 3351 farmland cells.
